drivingQuestion: Is the mishna's clause about 'pittin merubbot' redundant?
outcomeNote: The clause refers to excessively many small pieces, so it is not redundant.

segments.he: אוֹ שֶׁפְּתָתָן פִּתִּים מְרוּבּוֹת – כְּשֵׁרָה. הַשְׁתָּא לֹא פָּתַת כְּלָל – כְּשֵׁרָה, פִּתִּין מְרוּבּוֹת מִיבַּעְיָא? מַאי ״פִּתִּין מְרוּבּוֹת״? שֶׁרִיבָּה בִּפְתִיתִין.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «Or» if it happened «that» the priest «broke» the meal offerings that require breaking into «greater pieces [pittim merubbot]» than appropriate, the meal offering is «fit.» The Gemara asks: «Now» that it has already been stated in the mishna that if one «did not break» the loaves into pieces «at all» the meal offering is «fit, is» it «necessary» to state that if one broke the meal offering into «greater pieces» than appropriate the meal offering is fit? The Gemara answers: «What» does the expression «pittin merubbot» mean? It means «that he increased [ribba]» the amount of the meal offering’s «pieces» by breaking the loaves into many pieces that were each smaller than an olive-bulk.
